title: The Evolution supervisor maps three components to files that do not exist
evidence:
A check of every path in app.evolution.supervisor._COMPONENT_PATHS against the repository (git ls-files) on the base commit reports three paths that do not exist:
  DEAD windows-agent  windows-agent/DeviceService/Program.cs
  DEAD browser-worker services/browser/pagentos_browser/worker.py
  DEAD generated_skill var/evolution/skills/candidate/skill.py
Every other mapped path exists.

Why it matters: paths_for_component() feeds derive_risk_tier() and promotion_class_for(), and the map claims to name where a change would land. Measured with promotion_class_for on the base commit:
  windows-agent/DeviceService/Program.cs (dead)                        -> AUTO_CANARY, tier 2
  devices/windows-agent/src/PagentOS.DeviceService/Program.cs (real)   -> NEVER_AUTO_PROMOTE, tier 4
  services/browser/pagentos_browser/worker.py (dead)                   -> AUTO_CANARY, tier 2
  services/browser/browser_agent/worker.py (real)                      -> AUTO_CANARY, tier 2
  var/evolution/skills/candidate/skill.py (dead)                       -> AUTO_CANARY, tier 2
  skills/generated/x/1/src/x.py (a real generated-skill path)          -> AUTO_CANARY, tier 2
So the Windows agent is misclassified - tier 2 (AUTO_CANARY) instead of tier 4 (NEVER_AUTO_PROMOTE), because the risk table's rule ^devices/windows-agent/ never sees the dead path. The browser worker and the generated skill are NOT misclassified: the risk table has no rule for either, so both are tier 2 with the real path as with the dead one. Their paths must still be real, but a test must not assert any other tier for them.

Facts about where these components really live in the repository (from git ls-files):
  - the Windows device service entry point is devices/windows-agent/src/PagentOS.DeviceService/Program.cs
  - the browser worker is services/browser/browser_agent/worker.py
  - generated skills are published at runtime by EvolutionRuntime.skills_root under skills/generated/<skill>/<version>/src/<skill>.py; the directory skills/generated/ is tracked (it holds a README), its contents are generated and ignored, so a generated skill's file legitimately does not exist in a checkout.

The regression test must prove that every mapped path either exists in the repository or lies under a declared runtime-generated root, and that the Windows agent's component now classifies as NEVER_AUTO_PROMOTE (tier 4).
